1	---
2	name: caveman
3	description: >
4	  Ultra-compressed communication mode that cuts output tokens while keeping
5	  technical accuracy. Levels: lite, full, ultra and the wenyan variants. Use for
6	  /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief" or "less tokens".
7	---
8	
9	Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.
10	
11	## Persistence
12	
13	Default style for this whole session, every response, until user say "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Keep terse on long sessions no filler drift.
14	
15	Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.
16	
17	## Rules
18	
19	Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.
20	
21	Never drop not/never/no/only/except flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.
22	
23	Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.
24	
25	Clarity register: mix ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English into caveman, always. One idea per sentence. Sentence short, target 20 words max. Active voice. Present tense where true. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.
26	
27	Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.
28	
29	Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. text:
`bot.mjs` is written, and my check script passes. I ran it under three server time zones (UTC, Asia/Tokyo, America/Los_Angeles) with the same results. Nothing is sent.

The check script is `/tmp/bot-check/check.mjs`, outside the repo. It covers the 8:00 and 21:00 edges, both daylight-saving changes in Chicago, other zones, and each reason code.

## Rules, in the order checked

The first rule that fails sets the reason.

| Reason code | Applies to | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_now` | both | `now` is not a valid Date |
| `invalid_message` | both | message, kind, body or recipient is missing or malformed |
| `invalid_phone` | both | phone is not `+1` plus a valid US number (area code and exchange start 2–9) |
| `empty_body` | both | body is blank |
| `opted_out` | marketing | `optedOutAt` is set. 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10) requires honoring a revocation, and CTIA requires STOP to end messages. |
| `no_marketing_consent` | marketing | `marketingConsent` is not exactly `true`. This is the prior express written consent in 64.1200(a)(2). |
| `invalid_time_zone` | marketing | the time zone is missing or not a real IANA zone |
| `quiet_hours` | marketing | the customer's local time is before 8:00 or at 21:00 or later. This is 64.1200(c)(1). |
| `missing_opt_out_instructions` | marketing | the body does not contain the word STOP. This is the CTIA opt-out requirement. |

The local hour comes from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the customer's zone, so the server's own zone has no effect.

## Choices your lawyers should confirm

- **Opt-out takes effect immediately.** The FCC allows up to 10 business days, and CTIA expects it at once, so I block at once. A bad `optedOutAt` value also counts as opted out.
- **Transactional texts are allowed after STOP.** They skip the consent, opt-out and quiet-hours checks, because the customer triggered them. The FCC's "revoke-all" provision may cover them. I'm not certain of its current effective date. If counsel wants them blocked, add an `opted_out` check before the transactional return.
- **21:00:00 exactly is blocked.** The rule says "after 9 p.m.", so this is stricter than required.
- **A blank or invalid zone fails closed for marketing.**

## Not covered

- National Do-Not-Call registry and internal do-not-call lists, because the function has no data for them.
- Stricter state rules, such as Florida's 8:00–20:00 window and Maryland's. The function uses the federal 8:00–21:00 window.
- Detecting marketing content inside a message labeled transactional. A mixed message is legally telemarketing, and a label can't catch it.
- Sender identification in the body and the HELP keyword. The function only checks for STOP.
- The customer's actual location. The function uses the home time zone from the profile, as you specified.
